chunks: From him, from Ibn Faddal, from Al-Muthanna Al-Hannat, from Abdullah ibn Ajlan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
One who knows this Authority (Imamate) then dies before the Rising of the Qa'im (peace be upon him), for him is like the reward of one who fought alongside him.

key_terms.أَجۡر: Reward, specifically referring to the spiritual merit of martyrdom or fighting
key_terms.اَلْأَمْرُ: The Authority/Imamate, referring to the divine leadership of the Imams
key_terms.اَلْقَائِمُ: The Riser, a title for Imam Al-Mahdi (a.s.) who will rise to establish justice
key_terms.مَعَهُ: With him, referring to fighting alongside the Imam in his campaigns

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for a believer who dies before the appearance of Imam Mahdi?
ai.summary: In Shia eschatology, this hadith from Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores that spiritual recognition (*ma'rifah*) of the Imamate is the primary criterion for reward, superseding the need for physical participation in the Qa'im's military campaigns. Scholars interpret the 'like the reward of those who fought with him' as a metaphor for the high status of steadfast believers in the 'Great Occultation' (*al-Ghaybah al-Kubra*), who maintain their faith amidst trials. This elevates the spiritual merit of the pre-reappearance era to be comparable to the active struggle of the post-reappearance era.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 474 - It is narrated from Fadhl from Ibn Faddal from Muthanna Hannat from Abdullah bin Ajlan from Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s) that he said: “
One who believes in occultation and reappearance, but dies before the advent of Imam Mahdi (a.s) it is as if he has died fighting alongside the Imam.”
